content:
We have been on iOS 27 for a couple of months now. Of course, it's still in beta — it's still about four to six weeks away from a general release. That said, even though I've been running the beta on my phone for the past two months, I haven't really paid much attention to it. It just... works.

Of course, I still rush off to the software update screen to install the latest beta every couple of weeks or so. That's the only part of the beta experience that's consistent with cycle 27.

Beyond that, I can't come up with the usual things you'd say about a beta. Battery drain is basically nonexistent, the phone doesn't get hot, there haven't been a bunch of weird jank, and the phone isn't randomly respringing.

Running iOS 27 gets you all the benefits of new software — Siri AI, AirPods EQ, new Wallet tickets in Safari, beefier Photo AI editing, and more — without any of the problems you'd typically expect from running bleeding-edge beta software. Honestly, it's kind of remarkable.

Maybe it's also because iOS 26 was unstable to begin with. Especially iOS 26.5, which for some reason (at least for me) caused constant resprings on my phone.

Of course, these are all personal experiences, but ask just about anyone and you'll hear stories about iOS 26 not being great for them either.

iOS 27 is genuinely excellent

Overall, iOS 27 delivers on speed improvements, bug fixes, stability, and quality-of-life enhancements. You might not feel it right away because Siri AI is doing a lot of background indexing — but Apple already released iOS 26.6 earlier, so by the time you get to iOS 27, it'll have already started indexing for Siri AI in the background, so you don't have to do anything. Smooth sailing from there.

Top comment by Uno

While I largely agree that iOS 27 (and WatchOS 27) betas have been significantly more stable and battery-friendly than previous iOS betas, I have to disagree when it comes to Siri. In the two iOS/WatchOS 27 betas released so far, Siri has been essentially useless. Typing questions in the Siri app is fine, but using voice commands is incredibly frustrating and a complete waste of time.

Of course, this is purely based on my personal experience.

I'm very much looking forward to next month when iOS 27 officially rolls out to the general public. Even though it's a little hard to believe, Apple seems to have genuinely fixed most of iOS's major pain points. Of course, software is never going to be perfect — but this is hands-down the smoothest my iPhone has been in recent memory.

iOS 27 will support every iPhone model that supports iOS 26, going all the way back to the iPhone 11 and newer.
